name: Four Seasons Hotel Seoul
insider_take: Seoul's most sophisticated sanctuary sits above the bustling Gwanghwamun district, where modern luxury meets centuries of Korean heritage.
whats_special: This architectural marvel occupies floors 76-101 of the Northeast Asia Trade Tower, making it one of the world's highest Four Seasons properties. The hotel's signature spa features traditional Korean jade and gold treatments, while its restaurants serve both Michelin-starred cuisine and authentic Korean royal court dishes.
pro_tip: Book a room on floors 95+ for unobstructed views of Bukhansan National Park and the Han River. The sunrise views over the ancient palaces are absolutely breathtaking from this elevation.
dont_miss: The hotel's proximity to five UNESCO World Heritage palaces, including Gyeongbokgung and Changdeokgung, both within walking distance. Visit the rooftop bar at sunset for panoramic city views, then explore the underground Gwanghwamun Plaza's cultural exhibitions showcasing Korea's royal history.
pros: Prime Gangnam district location with easy access to shopping and business centers
Exceptional service standards with personalized attention and multilingual staff
Luxurious spa and wellness facilities with traditional Korean treatments
Outstanding dining options featuring both international and authentic Korean cuisine
cons: Limited outdoor recreational space due to urban location
